study.title: World's First Real-Time Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke

imaging.modality_detail: Intraprocedural biplane fluoroscopic images; the system can analyze either subtracted or unsubtracted images
imaging.territory_detail: Mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke with large vessel occlusion (MCA M1/M2, ICA, ACA A2, basilar)

task.task_description: Real-time tracking of guiding catheter, aspiration catheter and guidewire tips on biplane fluoroscopy with notifications when the guiding catheter moves out of view; notification precision, recall and clinical usefulness evaluated from procedure video recordings.
task.clinical_application: Intraprocedural assistance during mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke to prevent overlooking unintended guiding catheter movement

temporal_evidence.quote: triggering notifications only when the GC disappears from its previous visible position without associated field adjustments

metrics.metric: Precision of GC out of view notifications
Recall of GC out of view notifications
Clinically useful notifications among TP notifications

G1.quote: this study included a small number of cases performed at a single institution

G2.quote: Because AI tends to be vulnerable to atypical conditions, more studies on various situations are required.

G6.quote: Large prospective studies evaluating the system's effectiveness are warranted.

G11.quote: Largescale studies are warranted to validate its impact on procedural workflow and clinical outcomes.

other_limitations: Indirect verification of effectiveness; unclear whether operator noticed movement before notification
Only local anesthesia cases with balloon-mounted guiding catheters
Relatively low AIS case volume may have influenced notification numbers
Effect of AI on puncture-to-recanalization time not investigated
future_work: Larger comparative studies of P2R times with and without AI assistance
Assess impact by operator experience level
Operator timestamping of noticed events to compare with AI notifications
Evaluation under general anesthesia and with nonballoon guiding catheters
Large prospective studies of system effectiveness
